The experimental results show that the mAP @ 50 index of MSTD-Net on the three datasets reaches 7575 %, 9730 % and 7403 %, respectively. Compared with the baseline model YOLO26m, MSTD-Net increased mAP @ 50 by 100 %, 026 % and 792 % on DOTA15, UCAS-AOD and HRSC2016 datasets, respectively. The ablation experiment further verifies that the three improved modules all have gains in detection performance, but the improvement is different on different data sets.

nodes.name: Frontiers in Computing and Intelligent Systems
Improving Warehouse Operational Performance through Lean and VSM: Evidence from a Temperature-Controlled Logistics Facility
nodes.venue: International Journal of innovative inventions in Social Science and Humanities
nodes.abstract: This study investigates operational inefficiencies in a temperature-controlled warehouse by applying Lean principles and Value Stream Mapping (VSM) to analyze existing processes and develop improvement strategies. A case study was conducted at a cold storage warehouse in Thailand to examine warehouse operations, identify waste, and evaluate process and layout improvements. Data were collected through direct observation, process mapping, time measurement, and interviews with warehouse personnel. The Current State VSM revealed a sequential workflow consisting of receiving, put-away, storage, picking, and dispatch. The analysis showed that non-value-added activities accounted for 89.84% of the total lead time, with the storage stage representing the major source of delay and inventory accumulation. Additional waste was identified in motion and transportation due to inefficient warehouse layout and product placement. Based on these findings, a Future State VSM and an improved warehouse layout were developed by reorganizing storage locations using demand-based classification, reducing unnecessary travel, and standardizing operating procedures. The proposed improvements resulted in reductions in lead time, travel distance, and operational processing time while improving workflow continuity and warehouse efficiency. The findings demonstrate that integrating Lean principles with VSM and warehouse layout redesign provides an effective approach for identifying operational waste and enhancing the performance of temperature-controlled warehouse operations. The proposed framework offers practical guidance for warehouse managers seeking to improve operational efficiency and support continuous process improvement in cold chain logistics.

nodes.name: International Journal of innovative inventions in Social Science and Humanities
WeatherAgent-SAM: Text-Grounded Agentic Tool Selection for Robust SAM Segmentation
nodes.venue: Applied Sciences
nodes.abstract: The Segment Anything Model (SAM) provides a versatile promptable segmentation interface, but adverse weather and image degradation can obscure visual cues and substantially reduce its accuracy. Existing approaches mainly follow two directions to mitigate this issue. The first adapts SAM through fine-tuning or additional trainable modules, which requires model-side optimization. The second preprocesses degraded images before SAM inference, but such methods are generally optimized for perceptual restoration rather than downstream segmentation. We introduce WeatherAgent-SAM, an agentic framework that improves degraded-image segmentation through response-conditioned preprocessing selection while keeping SAM frozen. WeatherAgent-SAM takes SAM’s initial response and a spatial prompt as inputs and uses response-conditioned knowledge to determine which preprocessing method should be applied next. To realize this process, the framework comprises two key modules. First, Fine-Grained Response-Conditioned Knowledge Construction adopts a progressive coarse-to-fine strategy: it first categorizes SAM responses into recurring states and then explores how individual preprocessing methods affect segmentation within each state. This design enables the agent to distinguish methods that pursue similar enhancement objectives but produce different segmentation outcomes. Second, a learnable Mask Verifier estimates the quality of each resulting SAM mask without ground truth and provides feedback to the agent, allowing tool selection to proceed iteratively and stop when a satisfactory prediction is identified. Experiments demonstrate that WeatherAgent-SAM achieves results comparable to those of the evaluated baselines on the Robust-Seg dataset and outperforms SAM, RobustSAM, and GaRA-SAM-Syn on the ACDC dataset.

nodes.name: Unraveling Spatial Associations of Surface Subsidence in Typical Oil Production Areas of Songyuan City by Integrating Time-Series InSAR and Deep Learning
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Oilfield subsidence threatens infrastructure and sustainable development. Although facility detection, factor-association analysis, and deformation forecasting have each advanced considerably, their systematic integration remains insufficiently explored for oilfields in agricultural plains, where C-band SAR decorrelation over cropland and wetland yields sparse and uneven deformation observations. This constraint complicates facility extraction, quantitative analysis of associations among interacting factors, and robust temporal prediction. To address these challenges, this study develops and applies an integrated modular workflow for the monitoring, analysis and prediction of surface subsidence in a typical oil production area of Songyuan City, China. We first used PS-InSAR for high-precision deformation monitoring and validated the results with leveling survey data. Subsequently, the YOLOv12 model was utilized for automated oil well identification, and the Geodetector model was applied to quantify the spatial associations between subsidence and the examined natural and anthropogenic factors. Finally, a hybrid LSTM–Transformer model was developed for time-series prediction and applied to forecast deformation through November 2025, twelve months beyond the final SAR acquisition. Results indicate significant spatial differentiation in deformation, with a maximum subsidence rate of −26.0 mm/y. Analysis identifies oil well density and surface elevation as the leading spatial factors among those examined, and the buffer zone analysis indicates a distance-related association of approximately 700 m between oil wells and subsidence rates. The hybrid model demonstrated superior overall accuracy compared to standalone LSTM and Transformer models. The findings provide concrete scientific support for risk mitigation in oil cities.

nodes.name: Unified Embedding and Composable Fusion for Arbitrary Multimodal Person Re-Identification
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: Driven by the advancement of intelligent security, person re-identification has evolved from single-modality imagery to complex multimodal tasks involving infrared, text, sketches, and paintings. However, most existing methods are restricted to fixed modality pairs and struggle to accommodate the flexible fusion requirements of variable inputs, making the integration of arbitrary modality combinations a critical challenge. To address this, we propose the Unified Embedding Representation Fusion Network (UERF-Net), a framework based on unified embedding representation fusion. This method first establishes a unified embedding space to map heterogeneous modalities into a shared representation, effectively narrowing the modality gap through an explicit pre-alignment strategy. It then introduces a composable fusion mechanism utilizing a joint self-attention module to facilitate deep token-level interactions across diverse modality combinations. Furthermore, a distribution alignment strategy is employed to optimize similarity distributions via Supervised Distribution Alignment (SDA), significantly enhancing feature stability and identity discriminative power. Experimental results on the five-modality ORBench benchmark demonstrate that UERF-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance in Rank-1 accuracy (R1) and mean average precision (mAP), confirming the robustness and superior adaptability of our unified embedding-based modeling in complex, multi-source retrieval scenarios.

nodes.name: Trajectory-SAM: Object Trajectory-Guided Segmentation for Remote Sensing Videos
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: The rapid proliferation of high-resolution remote sensing video (RSV) has made object segmentation an increasingly critical yet challenging task. Existing methods face two fundamental limitations in this domain: (1) the intrinsic complexity of RSVs arising from diminutive object sizes, dense distributions, and drastic scale variations; (2) prohibitive computational overhead and latency caused by the massive spatial resolution of remote sensing imagery. To address these challenges, we propose Trajectory-SAM, a novel object trajectory-guided segmentation framework tailored for rapid and accurate object segmentation in RSVs. Specifically, we first employ a Graph Neural Network to extract representative keyframes, improving data utilization efficiency while suppressing attention drift and interpretation bias induced by redundant frames. We then introduce Temporal-LoRA, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy for the Segment Anything Model (SAM), substantially enhancing its spatiotemporal contextual understanding in remote sensing domains. Finally, we devise a sample-augmentation-based knowledge distillation strategy to accelerate inference without sacrificing segmentation quality. Extensive experiments on the SAT-MTB, iSAID, and VHR-10 datasets demonstrate that our proposed Trajectory-SAM achieves superior performance, establishing a compelling trade-off between accuracy and speed.

nodes.name: Spatial Overlap Between Wind Power Licensing Areas and Potential Grazing Lands in Greece: A National Screening Assessment
nodes.venue: Sustainability
nodes.abstract: Wind energy expansion constitutes a central component of Greece’s energy transition. However, the spatial allocation of Wind Power Production Plants (WPPs) may coincide with potential grazing lands and Natura 2000 protected areas, creating potential land-use and conservation interfaces that require careful planning. This study provides a national-scale spatial screening assessment of the overlap between WPP licensing areas and potential grazing lands in Greece. Geospatial data from the Regulatory Authority for Energy (RAE), retrieved in February 2026, were intersected with CORINE Land Cover 2018 data using GIS-based vector analysis. Four alternative grazing-land classification scenarios were applied to account for uncertainty in the spatial definition of potential grazing lands. A spatial intersection was conducted between WPP licensing areas and Natura 2000 boundaries, followed by an assessment of potential grazing-land overlap within the resulting WPP-Natura 2000 areas. The results showed that, across the four scenarios, 65.89% to 70.34% of the total WPP polygon area overlapped potential grazing lands, while overlap within individual licensing stages ranged from 63.40% to 85.93%. Approximately 28.64% of the total WPP polygon area was located within Natura 2000 sites. Within these WPP-Natura 2000 areas, the proportion classified as potential grazing land ranged from 62.68% to 72.19% across the four scenarios. Regional analysis further revealed marked variation in overlap intensity among NUTS-2 regions, licensing stages, and grazing-land scenarios, with producer-certification areas generally showing the highest regional intensities. Although WPP licensing polygons do not represent the actual physical footprint of wind turbines and associated infrastructure, their substantial spatial coincidence with potential grazing lands highlights an important interface between renewable-energy development, livestock farming activities, and biodiversity conservation. The study provides a first-order national-scale screening assessment that can support integrated spatial planning, grazing management, biodiversity conservation, and environmental permitting in Greece.

nodes.name: Simulation-based design and preliminary controller-level assessment of the real-time control logic of a proposed multimodal vibrotactile navigation belt
nodes.venue: Technology and Disability
nodes.abstract: Wearable assistive technologies for blind and visually impaired users require discreet feedback channels that do not rely primarily on continuous auditory output. This study presents a simulation-based proof of concept focused on the controller logic of a proposed multimodal vibrotactile navigation belt combining ultrasonic short-range obstacle detection, directional haptic feedback, and a discreet audio channel for high-priority events. The proposed architecture includes three HC-SR04 sensors, a light sensor, and a potentiometer for adjusting the distance threshold. The firmware, implemented in C on an STM32 microcontroller, uses separate threads for data acquisition, distance computation, event handling, and timing. The controller decision logic implemented in the simulation reference model was verified through deterministic unit testing, achieving 100% branch coverage. A Python simulator was then used to assess closed-loop controller–agent behavior in two-dimensional environments with obstacles and light variations. Across 30 base seeds and 30,000 episodes per condition, the mean collision rate was 0.978 ± 0.004 in the no-feedback baseline and 0.101 ± 0.008 in the controller-assisted condition, corresponding to a mean relative reduction of 89.70% ± 0.81%. These findings support controller-level technical feasibility but do not establish real-world usability, user effectiveness, or clinical benefit. Physical prototyping, calibration, and end-user evaluation remain necessary.

nodes.name: SF-SRGAN: Shift-Free Transformer GAN with High-Frequency Enhancement for Image Super-Resolution
nodes.venue: Computers
nodes.abstract: Image super-resolution refers to the process of recovering high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. However, existing methods face three critical challenges: GAN-based approaches suffer from training instability and artifacts; shifted-window Transformers have issues of computational cost and fixed receptive fields; and high-frequency detail modeling along with multi-source feature fusion remains insufficient. To address these issues, this paper proposes SF-SRGAN, a high-frequency enhanced shift-free Transformer generative adversarial network. The generator introduces a shift-free variable-window Transformer architecture that progressively increases window sizes across layers (4 × 4 → 8 × 8 → 16 × 16), achieving natural receptive field expansion without shift operations or masking overhead. A High-Frequency Positional Encoding module is designed to extract multi-directional high-frequency responses via Laplacian kernels and adaptively inject them through a content-aware gating mechanism. An adaptive dual-path fusion mechanism dynamically integrates global Transformer features with local CNN features. The discriminator adopts a multi-scale architecture combined with R1 gradient penalty and an auxiliary edge prediction loss to stabilize adversarial training and preserve high-frequency structures. Extensive experiments on SR-CelebA and Flickr2K datasets demonstrate that SF-SRGAN achieves superior performance in PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS, and ablation studies validate the effectiveness of each component.

nodes.name: Real-Time Physical-to-Virtual Scene Reconstruction for Dynamic Manufacturing Systems via Semantic—Spatial Mapping
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: Real-time reconstruction of virtual scenes in response to changing physical conditions remains a challenge in manufacturing digital-twin systems. During manufacturing operations, changes in object positions, orientations, and spatial arrangements require the virtual scene to be updated to reflect the evolving physical environment. Here, we present a physical-scene-driven semantic–spatial mapping framework to support real-time scene reconstruction in dynamic manufacturing systems. The framework integrates visual object detection, point-cloud-based spatial estimation, digital asset retrieval, and virtual scene updating. A lightweight detector identifies physical objects and provides semantic information for spatial processing, while object-level point clouds are used to estimate their positions and orientations. The resulting semantic and spatial information is associated with predefined computer-aided design (CAD) models and used to update corresponding virtual objects in a Unity environment. To improve the efficiency of semantic perception, we develop SF-Lite-YOLOv8n by integrating C2f_Star, Spectral-SPPF, and Detect_Efficient. On the MVTec ITODD dataset, the detector achieves an mAP@0.5 of 0.940 with 1.98 million parameters and 6.2 GFLOPs, at a measured inference speed of 83 frames per second. In experiments involving 20 self-collected manufacturing scenes, the integrated perception and mapping pipeline achieves mean position and orientation errors of 2.7 mm and 1.9°, respectively, with a processing latency of 146 ms, excluding Unity rendering. These results demonstrate the potential of combining lightweight semantic perception and point-cloud-based spatial estimation to support the reconstruction and updating of virtual manufacturing scenes.

nodes.name: Integrated Remote Sensing and Geological Analysis for Delineating Prospective Gold-Mineralisation Zones at the Suzdal Deposit, Kazakhstan
nodes.venue: Geosciences
nodes.abstract: Remote sensing can support mineral exploration in geologically complex terrains, but distinguishing mineralisation-associated spectral responses from lithological and surficial variability remains challenging. This study presents and evaluates an integrated workflow for delineating and prioritising prospective zones for gold mineralisation at the Suzdal deposit, Kazakhstan. Sentinel-2 imagery was analysed using diagnostic band ratios, unsupervised spectral clustering, principal component analysis (PCA), and reference-signature-based spectral similarity classification. The resulting spectral patterns were integrated with lithological contacts, structural–geomorphological features, residual structures, denudation patterns, and lineaments; the delineated prospective zones were subsequently evaluated using independent exploration-drilling data and supporting geophysical information. PCA highlighted broad multispectral variability, whereas spectral similarity classification provided more spatially explicit delineation of mineralisation-associated surface responses. Higher-priority zones were identified where complementary remotely sensed responses converged within favourable geological–structural domains. Quantitative validation showed that 6 of 7 assay-confirmed Au-positive drill holes occurred within the delineated prospective zones, corresponding to a Spatial Capture Rate (SCR) of 85.7%. The novelty lies in combining deposit-specific geological criteria with complementary Sentinel-2 analyses within a unified targeting framework and subsequently evaluating the resulting prospectivity pattern against independent exploration evidence. The workflow provides a reproducible approach for exploration-target prioritisation at Suzdal and potentially in comparable gold-mineralised settings in Kazakhstan.

nodes.name: Image-Based Quantitative Pore Analysis of Cementitious Materials: A Scale-Resolved Review of X-Ray CT Methods and Metrics
nodes.venue: Buildings
nodes.abstract: X-ray computed tomography (CT) has become the reference non-destructive technique for the three-dimensional characterization of the pore structures of cementitious materials. This review maps 140 application studies—spanning cement paste, mortar and concrete, from air-entrained, cellular and recycled-aggregate systems to alkali-activated binders, ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) and 3D-printed materials—and the underlying image-analysis methodology is inventoried separately and excluded from all frequency statistics. Each study is classified by voxel-size class (sub-micron, <1 µm; micro, 1–20 µm; meso, 20–100 µm; macro, >100 µm; multiscale), with voxel size being a sampling parameter rather than a spatial resolution, and by the pore metrics it reports under six metric families. The synthesis reveals similar concentrations at the micro (48/140) and meso (50/140) scales, a dominance of porosity and pore-size distribution at every scale, and pronounced under-use of higher-order shape and spatial statistics: flatness, elongation and pair-correlation functions each appear in less than 2% of studies. Systematic discrepancies between scales are analyzed: resolution-conditioned porosity, the representative elementary volume–resolution dilemma, segmentation-induced variance comparable to material effects, and the persistent CT–mercury intrusion porosity mismatch. Priorities are standardized segmentation benchmarks, scale-bridging registration protocols, routine uncertainty reporting and broader adoption of quantitative shape and spatial descriptors. Provisional assignments are flagged in the dataset.

nodes.name: Hypergraph-Augmented Reconstruction and Adaptive Metric Aggregation Network for Few-Shot Fine-Grained Image Classification
nodes.venue: Electronics
nodes.abstract: Few-shot fine-grained image classification aims to recognize unseen fine-grained categories from very few labeled examples. The task is difficult because visually similar classes may differ only in subtle details, while images from the same class can vary considerably. Useful evidence is therefore often localized. Reconstruction-based metric methods reduce local misalignment by reconstructing query features from class-wise support features, but a small support set may still provide an incomplete reconstruction basis. In addition, spatial reconstruction errors are usually combined with fixed or nearly uniform weights, and intermediate features receive no direct reconstruction-oriented supervision. We develop HARA, a Hypergraph-Augmented Reconstruction and Adaptive Metric Aggregation Network, to address these limitations. HARA forms learnable soft hyperedges over local support features and uses the resulting aggregated features to enrich the class-wise reconstruction basis. It then combines class-conditional reconstruction with query self-reconstruction to obtain position-wise joint errors, which are aggregated using query-dependent weights. A training-only auxiliary branch applies reconstruction-based supervision to intermediate backbone features. For 5-way evaluation, HARA obtains 84.09%/93.48% on CUB-200-2011, 76.91%/88.69% on Stanford Dogs and 88.53%/95.87% on Stanford Cars under the 1-shot/5-shot settings, respectively. Ablation and diagnostic analyses further characterize the contributions and behavior of the proposed framework. Overall, HARA provides an effective extension to reconstruction-based few-shot fine-grained classification.

nodes.name: From sensing to transforming: The discursive trajectory of AI and the limited prominence of human-centered engagement themes
nodes.venue: WORK: A Journal of Prevention, Assessment & Rehabilitation
nodes.abstract: Background Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption transformed work structures after 2022, raising psychological safety concerns as efficiency priorities overshadow human-centered employee wellbeing. Objective This longitudinal study investigates how engagement is framed as a corporate communication strategy in Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 technology firms during early large-scale AI adoption (2022–2024). Methods Using IRaMuTeQ, 150 S&P 500 corporate reports (2022–2024) underwent Reinert's Descending Hierarchical Classification, Correspondence Factorial Analysis, and similarity network analysis, employing chi-square ( χ 2 ) marker filtering. Results Findings reveal a three-stage trajectory mapping onto dynamic capabilities: initial sensing (2022), platform seizing (2023), and process transformation (2024). However, human-centered engagement language (meaningfulness, safety, vigor) remained structurally marginalized, failing to form a stable lexical cluster and framing participation strictly through technical integration. Conclusions Public discourse serves as a proxy for enacting dynamic capabilities. Practically, HR leaders should prospectively audit AI communications to ensure technical efficiency narratives do not displace human-centered and psychological safety registers.

nodes.name: WORK: A Journal of Prevention, Assessment & Rehabilitation
Effects of Combined La–Ce Rare-Earth Treatment on the Hot-Rolled Microstructure and Texture of High-Grade Non-Oriented Electrical Steel
nodes.venue: Metals
nodes.abstract: This study compares high-grade non-oriented electrical steels without rare-earth addition and with a La-Ce combined rare-earth treatment. Optical microscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), and electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) were used to characterize the hot-rolled microstructure, through-thickness texture, and local orientation heterogeneity. The investigated La-Ce specimen exhibited a smaller average as-cast grain size (1.2 mm versus 2.0 mm) and a smaller hot-rolled surface grain size (39.08 μm versus 57.39 μm), together with a smoother microstructural transition from fine surface grains to elongated center-layer deformation grains. XRD revealed pronounced through-thickness texture gradients in both specimens. After a non-negativity-constrained post-reconstruction correction of the exported harmonic ODFs, the maximum α-fiber orientation density was 2.830 and 2.573 at the surface, 4.223 and 4.521 at 1/4 thickness, and 36.995 and 16.636 at the center for the rare-earth-free and La-Ce specimens, respectively. The center-layer difference corresponds to an approximately 55.0% lower α-fiber maximum in the investigated La-Ce specimen. For the γ-fiber, peak and mean f(g) values increased modestly at the surface and more strongly at 1/4 thickness, whereas the sampled ideal center-layer γ-fiber in the La-Ce specimen reached the lower bound of the constrained ODF representation. EBSD-IPF, GOS, and KAM maps further revealed reduced long-range orientation continuity and finer spatial segmentation of deformation-related orientation heterogeneity in the La-Ce specimen. Overall, the results show that trace La-Ce treatment is associated with microstructural refinement and a pronounced redistribution of the hot-band deformation texture, particularly in the sheet center.

nodes.name: Defect-Induced Negative Cooperative Adsorption on Plasmonic Heterointerfaces for Anti-Saturation Sensing of Bulky Emerging Contaminants
nodes.venue: Analytical Chemistry
nodes.abstract: Abstract Bulky emerging contaminants readily induce premature interface saturation, fundamentally limiting photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensors from simultaneously achieving ultrahigh sensitivity and a wide dynamic range. Herein, a defect-induced Au-sensitized WO3@FeWO4 heterointerface is proposed for the anti-saturation detection of the bulky contaminant rifampicin (RFP). The simultaneous regulation of oxygen and tungsten vacancies controls Au nucleation, promoting the exposure of highly active Au (311) facets to generate spatially heterogeneous active sites. The synergistic coupling between the heterojunction and the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect significantly accelerates charge separation, producing a strong initial PEC response. Crucially, this defect-facet coupled interface governs the adsorption dynamics of bulky RFP. The preferential occupation of high-activity sites triggers pronounced steric hindrance and repulsion, leading to negative cooperative adsorption (Hill coefficient = 0.318). This negative-feedback behavior effectively delays saturation, maintaining continuous interfacial responsiveness. Consequently, the sensor achieves an ultrawide linear range (1 nM to 150 μM) and an ultralow detection limit (0.76 nM). Ultimately, this work provides a novel method for monitoring bulky contaminants with high sensitivity and a broad linear range, successfully realizing real water sample analysis on a portable platform.

nodes.name: DSFormer: An Enhanced Dual-Selective Fusion Transformer Framework for Hyperspectral Image Classification++
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Hyperspectral image classification requires joint modeling of spectral signatures and spatial structure. In patch-based classification, each input patch is assigned the label of its center pixel, although neighboring pixels may belong to different land-cover classes. This setting motivates coordinating shallow spatial features, contextual refinement within the patch, and supervision of the resulting representation. We propose DSFormer++, an enhanced framework based on the original Dual Selective Fusion Transformer Network (DSFormer). Shallow Feature Compensation (SFC) combines shallow and patch-embedded features through gated residual fusion before the backbone. The Collaborative Global–Local (CGL) module applies an additional refinement operation with shared parameters before token selection at two backbone stages. Pixel Contrastive Loss (PCL) uses center-pixel labels to supervise projected patch embeddings during training. The proposed method achieves overall accuracies of 96.50%, 97.60%, 95.35%, and 94.83% on the Pavia University, Houston13, Indian Pines, and WHU-HH datasets, respectively. Component comparisons and approximately parameter-matched controls characterize configuration-dependent effects. Numerical checks assess consistency between the stated operations and their implementation, and an additional Botswana experiment extends the evaluation to a satellite wetland and woodland scene.

nodes.name: Cross-linguistic affective iconicity
nodes.abstract: Whether relationships between word form and affect reflect shared human constraints or language-specific conventions remains largely unresolved. Addressing this, here we tested whether affective mappings learned in one language zero-shot predict estimations for the emotional dimensions of valence and arousal in another using 85,375 lexical entries from ten languages diverse in origin and culture across eight (sub)lexical representations spanning orthographic, phonological, articulatory, and distributional semantic information. Results revealed a strong semantic transfer, greater for valence than arousal, while form-based transfer was smaller but consistently above zero across all seven representations for arousal, with the strongest effects for articulatory features. Language-distance analyses further revealed that valence-related orthographic and phoneme-bigram transfer was stronger between more closely related languages, particularly genealogically and the modest correspondence between fitted form coefficients indicated that transferable prediction coexisted with differences in feature weighting across languages. These findings characterize affective iconicity as graded and representation-dependent: valence generalizes most strongly through distributional meaning, whereas arousal leaves a more consistent cross-linguistic trace in word form. This pattern motivates an account in which culturally and historically shaped evaluative mappings coexist with activation-related mappings that may draw more broadly on shared embodied constraints, connecting linguistic form with the conceptual organization of affective experience.

nodes.name: Critical Success Factors in Developing Regional Multimodal Transportation Hubs Through Public-Private Partnerships
nodes.venue: Sustainability
nodes.abstract: Regional multimodal transportation hubs are strategic infrastructures for enhancing intermodal connectivity, regional competitiveness, and supply-chain resilience. Their development through Public–Private Partnerships (PPPs), however, requires coordination across institutional, infrastructural, financial, technological, and stakeholder domains. This study examines stakeholder perceptions of the critical success factors (CSFs) influencing the planning and development of a potential regional multimodal logistics hub through a PPP-type governance arrangement in Central Macedonia, Greece. An exploratory qualitative design was employed, based on questionnaire responses from 23 stakeholders and professionals across public authorities, business organizations, logistics and transport companies, construction and engineering firms, consultancies, and transport-infrastructure organizations. Responses were analyzed using theoretically informed reflexive thematic analysis. Six interrelated themes emerged: location and accessibility; infrastructure and technology; institutional and legal framework; financial sustainability and investment environment; stakeholder legitimacy and regional development; and adaptive sustainability. Findings highlight Central Macedonia’s strategic geographic advantages, particularly Thessaloniki’s gateway position, while distinguishing geographic potential from operational readiness. Successful development depends on reliable multimodal infrastructure, digital interoperability, institutional coordination, regulatory stability, credible demand and financing, effective public–private cooperation, stakeholder legitimacy, and adaptive capacity. In the Central Macedonia case, perceived implementation readiness emerges from the interaction of these conditions rather than from any single factor in isolation.

nodes.name: Compressed Time, Narrow Space: The Visual-Temporal Aesthetics of Mobile Microdrama on ReelShort
nodes.venue: Mobile Media & Communication
nodes.abstract: The widespread adoption of digital platforms and mobile devices has significantly transformed audiovisual storytelling. Short-form mobile microdramas represent not only a new mode of distribution but also a narrative form that reorganizes cinematic time and space. While previous research has primarily focused on platform economies, audience engagement, and algorithmic circulation, the visual-temporal organization of mobile microdramas has received comparatively little attention from the perspective of quantitative film analysis. Addressing this gap, this study investigates how mobile microdramas reorganize cinematic form through temporal compression and spatial narrowing. A quantitative formal analysis was conducted on the first episodes of 10 ReelShort series representing different narrative tropes. The analysis examined average shot length (ASL), editing rhythm, shots per minute, shot-scale distribution, and the use of establishing shots. Shot boundaries were automatically identified using Adobe Premiere Pro's Scene Edit Detection tool, while shot scales and spatial indicators were analysed through qualitative coding. The findings show that an exceptionally short ASL of 2.31 s, together with the predominance of medium shots and the limited use of full/long shots and establishing shots, minimizes spatial exposition while privileging character-centred compositions and producing a dense visual rhythm optimized for smartphone viewing. The results suggest that ReelShort reorganizes cinematic form by simultaneously compressing cinematic time and narrowing cinematic space, extending long-term stylistic tendencies in film history while adapting them to the perceptual and technological conditions of vertically oriented mobile media.

nodes.name: Beyond site-specific archaeological prospection: Spectral-geometry reveals cross-site cropmark signals in satellite data
nodes.venue: PNAS Nexus
nodes.abstract: Abstract Remote sensing has long supported archaeological prospection, mainly through the detection of cropmarks, a key archaeological proxy expressed as spectral vegetation anomalies over subsurface features. Yet, cropmark detection is still assumed in the literature to be highly site-specific, governed by local agronomic and environmental conditions. Using multispectral Sentinel-2 data from three European archaeological sites, we show that models trained in one landscape can recover meaningful archaeological proxy signals in other locations. By relying strictly on satellite spectral signatures for training, our models achieve measurable cross-location transferability without incorporating ancillary environmental data. We find that cross-site performance arises not from geographic proximity but from the spectral-geometric similarity of vegetation responses, and that transferability is strongly directional. We quantify this relationship through a Directional Strength Score (DSS), derived from monthly subcluster distances under multiple norms, which captures directional geometric similarity and correlates strongly with machine-learning performance. To keep the analysis grounded in the underlying spectral signal, we relied on architecturally restrained nonlinear classifiers (SVM and constrained XGBoost) and used NDVI-identified phenophases to align training and evaluation with comparable seasonal windows. Taken together, these results demonstrate that partial, spectrally mediated cross-location cropmark detection is feasible and that the underlying vegetation responses exhibit stable spectral structure, with spectral geometry offering a clear interpretive lens on why these signals can transfer across sites. Leveraging globally harmonized satellite data, this approach offers a scalable complement to uneven historical aerial archives and supports systematic regional archaeological prioritization to be deployed within integrated archaeological workflows.

nodes.name: Artificial Intelligence, Foundation Models, and Digital Twins for Climate-Resilient Agriculture: A Review
nodes.venue: Intelligent Agriculture
nodes.abstract: Climate change, increasing food demand, and resource constraints are accelerating the transition from conventional precision agriculture toward smart, autonomous, and climate-resilient agricultural systems. Artificial intelligence (AI), foundation models, digital twins (DTs), the Internet of Things (IoT), remote sensing, edge–cloud computing, and big data analytics are emerging as key technologies for data-driven agricultural management. This review critically evaluates recent advances in AI-driven intelligent agriculture, with emphasis on machine learning, deep learning, explainable AI (XAI), generative and agentic AI, multimodal foundation models, and digital twins, together with the sensing and computing infrastructures required for their deployment. Relevant literature was identified using keywords related to AI, foundation models, digital twins, IoT, precision agriculture, and climate-resilient agriculture, with emphasis on recent peer-reviewed studies addressing technological applications, performance, limitations, challenges, and future prospects. The selected literature was critically synthesized to identify technological trends, knowledge gaps, and emerging research opportunities. The review highlights that the greatest potential of intelligent agriculture lies in integrating heterogeneous data from sensors, UAVs (unmanned aerial vehicles), satellites, weather systems, field operations, and agricultural knowledge to support context-aware prediction, decision-making, and autonomous action. However, data quality, model generalizability, explainability, interoperability, cybersecurity, computational requirements, and large-scale field validation remain major challenges. This review further develops an integrated perspective connecting AI, foundation models, multimodal data infrastructures, digital twins, and autonomous agricultural systems within a unified cyber-physical ecosystem. Future priorities include trustworthy AI, agentic decision-making, semantic interoperability, federated learning, continuous learning, and self-learning digital twins toward Agriculture 6.0.

nodes.name: An Optimized Audio–Visual Deepfake Detection Framework Using Mamba Vision Transformers with Linear Complexity
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: The rise of advanced deepfake technologies presents new challenges to media authenticity, making it harder to spot manipulated videos through traditional approaches. Current approaches have a quadratic time complexity O(n2), poor cross-dataset generalization with 20 to 35% accuracy degradation, and inadequate audio–visual fusion mechanisms. This paper presents Mamba-AVGuard, a novel audio–visual deepfake detection framework leveraging Mamba Vision Transformers with selective state-space modeling to achieve linear O(n) complexity within the Mamba encoder streams. The novel framework combines a 12-layer visual Mamba encoder for spatial and temporal facial inconsistency analysis with an 8-layer lightweight audio Mamba encoder for prosodic inconsistency analysis, fused via a cross-modal attention block with ±33 ms temporal synchronization. Experiments conducted on two large-scale audio–visual deepfake benchmarks, FakeAVCeleb and AV-Deepfake1M, demonstrate that Mamba-AVGuard outperforms compared methods with 99.92% in-dataset accuracy and 98.47% cross-dataset accuracy on these two benchmarks. The system achieves a processing speed of less than 1.8 s for 30-s videos, with 56% less memory than the best competing transformer-based method, facilitating a throughput of more than 1200 videos per hour for social media verification and forensic workstations.

nodes.name: AMSSE-SwinTrans: A harmonized multimodal hybrid framework with explainable AI for ischemic stroke lesion segmentation
nodes.venue: Technology and Health Care
nodes.abstract: Background Accurate ischemic stroke lesion segmentation from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is important but challenging due to variability in lesion morphology. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) effectively capture local spatial features but often struggle to capture long-range contextual dependencies needed for irregular lesions. Transformer-based architectures are good at capturing global context; however, they are computationally expensive and difficult to deploy in resource-constrained environments. The black-box nature of deep learning models limits their clinical adoption owing to lack of transparency. Objective This study introduces AMSSE-SwinTrans, a lightweight hybrid CNN-Transformer framework to make stroke lesion segmentation accurate, efficient and interpretable across different MRI modalities. Methods This study proposes AMSSE-SwinTrans, a lightweight hybrid CNN-Transformer framework that combines adaptive multi-scale squeeze-and-excitation (AMSSE) module with simplified transformer blocks employing multi-head self-attention, along with explainable AI (XAI) for clinical interpretation. The model was evaluated on a single-channel harmonized multimodal two-dimensional MRI Slices from ATLAS v2.0 and ISLES 2022 dataset. Results The model achieved an overall Dice of 0.8629, lesion-specific Dice of 0.7535. An ablation study demonstrated a significant performance improvement when each component was added. The model comparisons were all significant with Wilcoxon signed-rank test yielding p-value ( p < 0.001) across all comparisons. With only 27.67 M parameters, 17.67 GFLOPs, and 9.22 ms inference time per slice, the architecture is well-suited for deployment in resource-constrained clinical settings. The interpretability of the model is supported by Attention Rollout and Grad-CAM++ visualizations. Conclusion AMSSE-SwinTrans establishes itself as a resource-efficient and interpretable framework for multimodal stroke lesion segmentation.

nodes.name: AI-Based Driver Drowsiness Detection Using Image Enhancement and Swin Transformer
nodes.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
nodes.abstract: This study introduces a smart system designed to detect driver drowsiness in real time, focusing mainly on checking whether a driver's eyes are closed for an unusually long period. While conventional AI image detection methods (like standard CNNs) often fail when faced with poor lighting, motion blur, noisy images, or deliberate visual distortions (adversarial attacks), this solution solves these issues by combining two advanced techniques: Diffusion-Based Denoising (U-Net Architecture): Acts as a preprocessing cleanup layer. Before analyzing the image, it strips away visual noise, blur, and distortion, turning corrupted camera frames into clear, high-quality images. Swin Transformer Model: Serves as the primary classification engine. It uses a multi-scale, window-based attention mechanism to accurately detect eye states (open vs. closed) across both fullface images and close-up eye patches. To make the AI more resilient to unpredictable driving conditions, the researchers trained it using artificial image modifications (like rotation, zooming, and shifting) along with simulated visual attacks.

nodes.name: Shravani Suresh Kutal, P. A. Sawant, Dr. H. B. Jadhav
A Review of Machine Learning in Species Distribution Modeling under Climate Change in West Africa
nodes.venue: Asian Journal of Geographical Research
nodes.abstract: Species distribution modelling (SDM) has become a central instrument for anticipating how biodiversity is redistributed under climate change, and machine learning now supplies most of the algorithmic capacity behind these predictions. West Africa combines high climatic exposure, dense reliance on wild biological resources, and thin biodiversity records, so the region is a demanding setting in which the strengths and weaknesses of machine learning SDMs are exposed. Scope. Peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2026 were synthesised to describe how correlative SDMs, tree-based ensembles, and deep learning have been applied to West African flora, fauna, disease vectors, and agricultural pests, and to assess the treatment of data quality, model transferability, and reporting standards. Key findings. Maximum entropy modelling remains the dominant approach, yet tree-based ensembles and, more recently, deep neural networks are being adopted where occurrence volume permits. Reported discrimination is high across algorithm families, with area under the curve values frequently above 0.90, though internal validation was shown to overstate reliability when sampling bias and extrapolation into novel climates were left uncorrected. Plant studies concentrated in Benin, Togo, Nigeria, and Burkina Faso projected habitat contraction for a majority of exploited woody species, with northward and upslope displacement of suitable conditions, while vector and pest models projected expansion of climatically suitable areas for several malaria vectors and invasive insects across the region. Persistent occurrence-data scarcity, spatial sampling bias, and inconsistent reporting were identified as the leading constraints on inference. Implications. Bias-aware calibration, spatially independent validation, standardised reporting, and investment in regional occurrence data are needed before machine learning SDMs are used to guide conservation prioritisation, protected-area design, and public-health planning in West Africa. This review positions the regional evidence within methodological developments and defines data-supported priorities for the next phase of work.

nodes.name: A Point Cloud Transformer-Based Regression Approach for Estimating Above-Ground Biomass from 3D Point Clouds
nodes.venue: Engineering Perspective
nodes.abstract: From the perspective of global food security, the estimation of crop biomass and yield is a critical process. Traditionally, plant height is manually measured using field samples for biomass and yield estimation, and plant samples are cut, dried, and weighed. This labor-intensive process can be made more efficient through advanced technologies integrated into modern agricultural machinery. One such technology, light detection and ranging (LiDAR), provides nondestructive 3D point clouds with millimeter-level accuracy. However, processing this data is highly challenging due to the complex canopy architecture of cereal crops. Therefore, deep learning architectures can be used to effectively analyze 3D point cloud data. In this context, a deep learning-based regression approach was proposed to estimate above-ground biomass from 3D point cloud data. This study employed a point cloud transformer (PCT) architecture. Growth Stage-PCT (GS-PCT) models were developed by integrating growth stage information into the proposed Small, Base, and Deep variants of the PCT architecture. According to the experimental results, when both growth stages were evaluated together, the proposed GS-PCT-Small model achieved the best performance, with an R² of 0.95, an RMSE of 88.60 g m⁻², an MAE of 69.34 g m⁻², and a MAPE of 13.69%. During the vegetative stage, the PCT-Small model achieved an RMSE of 58.52 g m⁻², while during the flowering stage, the GS-PCT-Small model achieved an RMSE of 111.55 g m⁻². The findings indicate that the models achieved high predictive performance for above-ground biomass estimation from 3D point clouds.

nodes.name: A Hierarchical Framework for Arctic Shoreline Type Mapping Using SAR and Optical Satellite Imagery
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Although intertidal-zone delineation and shoreline or coastal geomorphological classification have been extensively investigated, relatively few studies have integrated these complementary information layers within a unified and operational remote-sensing framework for oil-spill emergency response. With increasing development and marine transportation activities in the Arctic, detailed and spatially explicit shoreline information is essential for oil-spill response planning and coastal hazard assessment along the Canadian Arctic coast. A key challenge is to reliably characterize the spatial extent and geomorphological variability of Arctic intertidal shorelines under substantial temporal variability in tidal inundation and environmental conditions. This study presents a hierarchical shoreline classification framework designed to support oil-spill emergency preparedness and response planning. The framework integrates Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) backscatter, temporal-change and structural descriptors, and Sentinel-2 water-sensitive indices to derive a composite shore-zone proxy that captures spatial and temporal information on tidal inundation and coastal surface characteristics. This proxy supports Level 1 shore-zone mapping, while high-resolution optical imagery enables subsequent Level 2 shoreline-type classification. The framework was evaluated in four Canadian Arctic coastal areas representing diverse coastal landscapes and environmental conditions, including differences in tidal regimes, water turbidity, floating ice, and geomorphology. Results indicated that mapping accuracy remains constrained for tidal zones and substrates smaller than or comparable to the sensor’s spatial resolution. For Level 1 shore-zone mapping, unsupervised classification of the temporal and composite indices achieved overall mapping accuracies of 56–73% for the Upper Shore Zone across three study areas. For Level 2 shoreline-type mapping, Random Forest classification of high-resolution satellite imagery, including WorldView and GeoEye imagery, achieved overall accuracies of 81–85% across the four study areas. These results demonstrate the potential of the composite shore-zone proxy to integrate complementary SAR and optical information for consistent characterization of Arctic shore zones, while the subsequent shoreline-type classification provides additional geomorphological detail. Together, the hierarchical products provide spatially explicit shoreline information that can support the identification and prioritization of shoreline areas for oil-spill response planning and resource allocation.

nodes.name: Spatial transcriptomics elucidates trajectories associated with transformation in malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors
nodes.venue: Neuro-Oncology
nodes.abstract: Abstract Background Tumor invasion and malignant transformation are spatiotemporally coordinated processes that shape clinical behavior, diagnostic classification, and treatment response. Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs) are aggressive tumors that can arise sporadically or in people with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF-1) yet how distinct spatial niches underlie MPNST intra-tumor heterogeneity, local invasion or malignant transformation from benign precursors are not fully understood. Methods We integrate spatial analysis of 50,896 transcriptomes from 15 human MPNSTs with deep learning image analysis to define the interplay between genetic alterations, the immune microenvironment, and epigenetic cell fate regulation in MPNST invasion and transformation. Results Spatial transcriptomics reveal distinct infiltrating immune cells and immunomodulatory spatial clusters in sporadic compared to NF-1 associated MPNSTs. Local invasion is marked by spatially defined immunomodulatory and dedifferentiation programs. Analysis of two NF-1 associated MPNSTs with contiguous morphologically defined neurofibroma and MPNST components demonstrates NF-1 associated tumors identified a similar malignant transformation process associated with dynamic immune infiltration, chromosome 9p loss, and dedifferentiation concomitant with increased cell proliferation. Finally, deep learning morphology encoders were trained on spatial transcriptomic data to predict spatial transcriptomic cluster identity and chromosome 9p loss from hematoxylin and eosin stained (H&E) images although the generalizability of such encoders remains a challenge. Conclusions Our data provide a spatial framework for peripheral nerve sheath tumor transformation although the limited sample size of the present cohort will require additional validation of the proposed model.

nodes.name: Phenology-driven multisensor unsupervised crop mapping in data-scarce irrigated agriculture: a case of Adea District in Ethiopia
nodes.venue: Water Practice & Technology
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate irrigation planning, water allocation, and agricultural productivity assessment are frequently constrained in data-scare regions where reliable ground-based crop information and spatial coverage data are limited. This study addresses these gaps using a phenology-driven, multisensor unsupervised crop-mapping framework implemented within Google Earth Engine (GEE). The approach integrates monthly normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) profiles from Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1VV backscatter, and digital elevation model–derived terrain slope into unsupervised K-means clustering algorithm. Adea District, Ethiopia, served as a demonstration site to evaluate and interpret the phenological signatures of key irrigated crops. The identified crop types were mapped to estimate spatial coverage and compared with the ground truth observations of irrigated wheat and tomato fields. The approach successfully distinguished irrigated wheat and tomato fields with an overall classification accuracy of 91%, a Kappa coefficient of 0.82, and estimated cultivated areas of 666.93 and 812.35 ha, respectively. Combining phenological profiles with multisensor satellite observations significantly enhance unsupervised classification performance in heterogeneous, smallholder-dominated agricultural landscapes. The cloud-based framework offers a computationally scalable and cost-effective solution for crop mapping, and water productivity monitoring in data-scarce agricultural regions.
